mainTopic: Honest selling: mixing produce and wine, fair competition, and not dressing up merchandise
overview: This amud is about honest selling. The משנה forbids mixing new produce with old, and the ברייתא adds that this holds even when the old produce is the cheaper one. Mixing strong wine into weak wine is allowed because it improves the wine. רבי אלעזר learns from this that every 'באמת אמרו' is settled הלכה, and רב נחמן limits the permission to the winepress stage. The גמרא then explains why people mix wine nowadays: either buyers know and forgive it, or the משנה follows רבי אחא, who allows mixing anything that is tasted before buying. רב יהודה explains that the ban on sediment means sediment from a different day's wine, and a ברייתא supports him. רבא sends obviously diluted wine back to a store, and he defends this against אביי. Where diluting wine is the custom, it is allowed in set amounts, and רב limits this to the winepress stage. A new משנה discusses fair competition and not making goods look better than they are, and the גמרא begins explaining the reasons of the חכמים.

steps.title: Certainly not new produce with old
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its rule against mixing produce. If mixing new with new is forbidden, mixing new with old is obviously forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is no need to say that one may not mix new produce with old produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is completing a rule that started just before this: a seller may not mix produce, even new with new. Here it adds that new with old is obviously forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'there is no need to say' marks a case that is even more obvious than the one before it. Old produce is usually worth more, so mixing in new produce plainly cheats the buyer, who thinks he is getting all old.

keyTerms.meaning: And there is no need to say; this case is even more obvious
New produce, from this year's harvest
Old produce, from an earlier harvest

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a sentence that began earlier in the משנה ('one may not mix produce with produce, even new with new'). Don't read it as a standalone rule.

phrases.english: And there is no need to say,
new produce with old produce.
phrases.notes: Supply 'one may not mix.' The משנה leaves it out because it just said it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה's prohibition against mixing produce, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixing new produce with old produce for sale is certainly forbidden.

steps.title: Strong wine may be mixed with weak wine
steps.stepSummary: An exception: with wine, mixing strong into weak is allowed, because it makes the wine better.
steps.simpleTranslation: In truth they said: with wine, they allowed mixing strong wine with weak wine, because it improves it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives an exception to the ban on mixing. With wine, a seller may mix strong wine into weak wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on mixing exists so the buyer is not cheated. Here mixing actually improves the weaker wine, so the buyer is helped and not harmed. The opening words 'באמת אמרו' introduce this as a set, accepted rule.

keyTerms.meaning: In truth they said; an opening that introduces a fixed, accepted rule

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the reason behind the whole mixing ban. Mixing is forbidden when it harms the buyer, and allowed when it helps him.

phrases.english: In truth they said:
with wine, they permitted mixing strong with weak,
because it improves it.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the weak wine. Adding the strong wine makes it better.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an exception to the mixing ban from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixing strong wine into weak wine is permitted because it improves the wine.

steps.title: Wine sediment: don't add it, but you may leave it
steps.stepSummary: A seller may not add sediment into wine on purpose. He may sell wine together with its own natural sediment.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not mix wine sediment into wine, but he may give the buyer the wine's own sediment.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets a limit on wine. Putting sediment into wine on purpose is forbidden, but the seller does not have to strain out the sediment that is already there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding sediment on purpose fills the buyer's measure with something worthless, which is cheating. The sediment that belongs to the wine is a normal part of what the buyer expects, so leaving it in is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine sediment, the dregs that settle at the bottom

phrases.english: One may not mix wine sediment into wine,
but he may give him its sediment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After allowing one kind of wine mixing, the משנה sets a limit on another kind.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Adding sediment to wine on purpose is forbidden. Selling wine with its own sediment is allowed.

steps.title: Watered wine: tell the buyer, and never sell it to a merchant
steps.stepSummary: Wine that got water in it may be sold in a store only if the buyer is told. It may not be sold to a merchant at all, even if he is told.
steps.simpleTranslation: If water got mixed into someone's wine, he may not sell it in a store unless he tells the buyer. And he may not sell it to a merchant even if he tells him, because the merchant will only use it to deceive others.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules on wine that has water in it. A store customer must be told, and a merchant may not be sold it at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling the buyer removes the cheating, since he knows what he is getting. A merchant (תגר) buys in order to resell, and he will probably not tell his own customers. So telling the merchant doesn't help, because the wine will still end up deceiving someone.

keyTerms.meaning: Merchant, someone who buys to resell

steps.confusionAlert: Telling the buyer is enough in a store but not with a merchant. The problem with the merchant is not him; it is the customers he will sell to later.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that a seller is responsible not only for his own honesty but also for not passing along goods that will be used to cheat others.

phrases.english: One whose wine had water mixed into it,
may not sell it in the store,
unless he informed him.
And not to a merchant,
even though he informed him,
because it is only for deceiving with it.
phrases.notes: The merchant will resell it and probably won't tell his customers about the water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from mixing wine with wine or sediment to wine that has water mixed in.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Watered wine may be sold in a store only with disclosure, and never to a merchant, even with disclosure.

steps.title: Where watering wine is the custom, it is allowed
steps.stepSummary: In a place where people normally add water to wine, a seller may add water.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a place where people are used to putting water into wine, they may put it in.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds an exception based on local custom. Where everyone waters wine, doing so is not cheating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cheating means the buyer gets something different from what he expects. When adding water is the known local practice, buyers already expect it, so nobody is fooled.

keyTerms.meaning: A place where it is the custom

steps.whatToRemember: All the wine rules follow one idea: what matters is whether the buyer is misled. Improving the wine, leaving its natural sediment, telling the buyer, or following known local custom are all allowed, because no one is fooled.

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לְהָטִיל מַיִם בַּיַּיִן – יָטִילוּ.
phrases.english: A place where they are accustomed to put water into wine, they may put it in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an exception, based on local custom, to the watered-wine rule in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where adding water to wine is the custom, it is permitted.

steps.title: A merchant may combine produce from several sources
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends this topic with a merchant: he may pool grain from five threshing floors, or wine from five winepresses, as long as he is not trying to mix bad into good.
steps.simpleTranslation: A merchant may take grain from five threshing floors and put it into one storehouse, and wine from five winepresses and put it into one large barrel, as long as he does not intend to mix.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה's last clause on mixing allows a merchant (תגר) to combine merchandise bought from different people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows a merchant buys from many sources, so his customers expect his stock to be combined. This is different from a farmer selling his own field's produce, whose buyer expects one source. The condition is that the merchant may not plan to hide poor merchandise inside good merchandise.

keyTerms.meaning: Threshing floors, where grain is processed
A large wine barrel or cask

steps.confusionAlert: Here the merchant is allowed to combine stock, but in step 4 he was the one we worried would cheat. The difference is that his customers expect mixed stock, as long as he isn't purposely hiding bad merchandise among good.
steps.whatToRemember: A merchant may pool merchandise from different sources because buyers expect it. Purposely mixing to hide poor quality is still forbidden.

phrases.english: A merchant may take from five threshing floors
and put it into one storehouse,

phrases.aramaic: מֵחָמֵשׁ גִּתּוֹת וְנוֹתֵן לְתוֹךְ פִּיטוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: from five winepresses and put it into one large barrel,
provided that he does not intend to mix.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה's closing clause limits the mixing ban: a merchant who buys from many sources may combine them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A merchant may combine produce or wine from several sources into one container, as long as he does not intend to mix inferior merchandise into superior.

steps.title: Even cheaper old produce may not be mixed into new
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that you may not mix new and old produce at all, even when the old produce is the cheaper one, because buyers want new produce for storing.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The חכמים taught: Obviously, if new produce sells at four measures per coin and old at three (so old costs more), you may not mix them. But even if new sells at three and old at four (so new costs more), you still may not mix them, because people want produce they can store for a long time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that explains and widens the משנה's rule against mixing new and old produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The easy case is mixing cheap new produce into expensive old produce, because that is plain cheating. The ברייתא adds the harder case. Even when old produce is cheaper, mixing it into new produce is still cheating, because a buyer may want new produce that keeps longer in storage.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not necessary to say: the obvious case comes first, then the bigger חידוש
New produce from this year's crop
Old produce from last year's crop
To age them, meaning to keep them in storage

steps.confusionAlert: The numbers tell you how many measures you get for one coin. So 'four' means cheaper and 'three' means more expensive, not the other way around.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Sages taught:
It is not necessary to say
that when new produce is at four and old produce is at three
phrases.notes: He means four or three measures for one coin. More measures per coin means the produce is cheaper.

phrases.english: one may not mix them,
rather, even when new produce is at three
and old produce is at four, one may not mix them,
because a person wants to age them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה by quoting a ברייתא that widens the משנה's ban on mixing new and old produce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixing new and old produce is forbidden in both directions, even when the old produce is cheaper, because new produce is wanted for storage.

steps.title: Every 'באמת אמרו' is settled הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's wine exception. רבי אלעזר learns from its opening words that any rule introduced with 'באמת אמרו' is firm הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Actually, they said: with wine they allowed mixing strong into weak, because it makes the wine better.' רבי אלעזר said: This shows that every rule that begins 'Actually, they said' is established הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה about mixing wine. רבי אלעזר then comments on the phrase that opens it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine rule is an exception to the general ban on mixing, yet the משנה states it with full confidence. רבי אלעזר turns this into a general rule. Wherever a teaching begins with 'באמת אמרו', it is a firm, accepted הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, they said: an opening phrase for a firm ruling
This says: introduces a general lesson learned from the text

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a rule for reading משניות throughout ש״ס: the phrase 'באמת אמרו' marks a settled הלכה.

phrases.english: Actually, they said:
with wine they permitted
mixing strong wine into weak wine,
because it improves it, etc.
Rabbi Elazar said:
This says,
every 'actually, they said' is an established halacha.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא on produce to the משנה's exception for wine, and comments on its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any teaching introduced with 'באמת אמרו' is settled הלכה.

steps.title: The wine exception applies only in the winepress
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן limits the permission to mix wines to the time when the wine is still in the winepresses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The permission to mix wines was taught only for wine that is still in the winepresses.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן narrows the משנה's wine exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the exception is that mixing improves the wine. רב נחמן teaches that this only holds while the wine is still in the winepress. Once it has left the press, mixing would go back under the general ban.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught: refers back to the משנה's ruling

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
And they taught this only among the winepresses.
phrases.notes: He means while the wine is still in the press, before it has finished fermenting. That is when mixing helps it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: וּבֵין הַגִּיתּוֹת שָׁנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the wine exception just quoted from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixing strong wine into weak wine is allowed only while the wine is in the winepresses.

steps.title: Why do people mix wine nowadays outside the winepress?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that people today mix wine even after it leaves the winepress, which seems to go against רב נחמן's limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But nowadays people mix wine even when it is not in the winepresses. How is that allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's limit by pointing to what people actually do today. It sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the exception only applies in the winepress, then mixing later should count as cheating. Yet it is common practice. So the גמרא needs a reason why this practice is allowed.

phrases.english: But nowadays,
when people mix even not among the winepresses, how is that allowed?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִידָּנָא דְּקָא מְעָרְבִי שֶׁלֹּא בֵּין הַגִּיתּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's limit by pointing to common practice.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule that wine may be mixed only in the winepress
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Common practice today is to mix wine outside the press, which רב נחמן's rule seems to forbid.

steps.title: Buyers know about it and forgive it
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that today's practice is allowed because buyers know wine gets mixed and do not mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Because the buyers know about it and forgive it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question: mixing is allowed today because buyers know about it and accept it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cheating means the buyer is fooled. When everyone knows the custom of mixing and accepts it, no one is being fooled. So the practice is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: They forgive, give up their claim

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Because the buyers know and forgive it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: דְּיָדְעִי וְקָא מָחֲלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about today's practice.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual explanation: buyers know and give up their claim
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mixing outside the winepress would count as cheating.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is not cheating, since buyers know about it and accept it.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי אחא
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא answers differently. Our משנה follows רבי אחא, who allows mixing anything the buyer can taste before buying, so mixing wine is allowed even outside the winepress.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא said: Whose view is this משנה? It is רבי אחא's, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי אחא permits mixing something that gets tasted before it is bought.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives another reason why mixing wine today is allowed. He says it follows the opinion of רבי אחא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine is tasted before it is bought, so the buyer can judge it himself. Then mixing does not fool him, and רבי אחא allows it. This answer depends on the buyer's own tasting, not on a general custom of forgiving.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that is tasted before buying

steps.whatToRemember: Mixing wine is allowed in the winepress because it improves the wine (רב נחמן). Today it is allowed even outside the press, either because buyers know and forgive (רב פפא), or because wine is tasted before buying (רבי אחא).

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Ika, said:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Acha's,
as it is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Acha permits mixing with something that is tasted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא אָמַר: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי אַחָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the question in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the practice to a specific תנא (רבי אחא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mixing wine outside the winepress has no basis to be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: It follows רבי אחא, who allows mixing items the buyer tastes before buying.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה's rule on wine sediment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: you may not mix wine sediment into wine, but you may give the buyer its sediment.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: You may not mix wine dregs into wine, but you may give the buyer its dregs, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about wine sediment (the dregs that settle at the bottom). This is a setup line, and the next step will point out a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line has two parts. The first part forbids mixing sediment into wine. The second part allows giving the buyer 'his sediment.' These two parts seem to pull against each other, and the גמרא is about to ask about that.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine sediment, the dregs that settle at the bottom of the barrel

phrases.english: And one may not mix wine sediment into wine,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נוֹתֵן לוֹ אֶת שְׁמָרָיו וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: but he may give him its sediment, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of mixing wines to the next clause of the משנה, about sediment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mixing sediment into wine is forbidden, but giving the buyer his wine's sediment is allowed.

steps.title: The two halves of the sediment rule seem to contradict
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the first half said you may not mix sediment at all, so how can the second half allow giving it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But you just said in the first part that you may not mix sediment at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction inside the same line of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא forbids mixing sediment completely. But 'he gives him its sediment' sounds like handing the buyer sediment along with the wine, which is basically mixing it in. So which is it?

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה

phrases.english: But didn't you say in the first part
one may not mix at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the משנה quoted in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to 'give him its sediment'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full ban on mixing sediment cannot sit next to a permission to give sediment to the buyer.

steps.title: A suggested answer: he tells the buyer
steps.stepSummary: Maybe 'he gives him its sediment' means he may do it only if he tells the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: what does 'he gives him its sediment' mean? It means he tells the buyer about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible answer: the permission applies only when the seller tells the buyer there is sediment. The very next step will reject this idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading there is no contradiction. Secretly mixing in sediment is forbidden, and mixing it in openly, after telling the buyer, is allowed. The question is whether the rest of the משנה fits this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you say', which brings in a possible answer

phrases.english: And if you say
what does 'he gives him its sediment' mean?
that he informs him,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא מַאי נוֹתֵן לוֹ אֶת שְׁמָרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible way out of the contradiction raised in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: secretly versus openly
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two halves of the משנה contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Mixing is forbidden without telling the buyer and allowed after telling him.

steps.title: The last part of the משנה rules out that answer
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא makes 'telling the buyer' a separate, later rule, so the רישא must be speaking even about a case where he does not tell.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the last part of the משנה teaches: he may not sell it in a store unless he tells the buyer, and not to a merchant even if he tells him. This shows that the first part applies even when he does not tell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggested answer. The סיפא brings up 'telling the buyer' as something new, so the earlier permission cannot have depended on telling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רישא already meant 'only when you tell him,' the סיפא would not need to bring up telling as a new condition. Because the סיפא adds it, the רישא's permission must hold even without telling. So the contradiction from step 14 is back.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of the משנה
A merchant who buys in order to resell
'It follows that', a conclusion drawn from what the text implies

phrases.english: But from the fact that the last part teaches:
He may not sell it in the store
unless he informs him,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא לַתַּגָּר אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמּוֹדִיעוֹ,
phrases.english: and not to a merchant even if he informs him,
it follows that the first part

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מוֹדַע לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: applies even if he does not inform him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the answer offered in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole 'he tells the buyer' reading
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The סיפא treats telling the buyer as a new condition, so the רישא cannot already depend on it.

steps.title: רב יהודה: no mixing sediment from different days
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the ban is on mixing one day's sediment into another day's wine, while giving a wine's own sediment is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: This is what the משנה means. You may not mix last night's sediment into today's wine, or today's sediment into last night's wine. But you may give the buyer the sediment of his own wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה solves the contradiction by reading each half of the משנה as talking about different sediment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden 'mixing' means adding sediment that came from a different batch, which is foreign to this wine. 'His sediment' means the dregs that naturally belong to the wine being sold. The two halves no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it means', a reinterpretation of the text

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: This is what it means:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְעָרְבִין שְׁמָרִים שֶׁל אֶמֶשׁ בְּשֶׁל יוֹם,
phrases.english: one may not mix sediment of last night with that of today,
nor that of today with that of last night.
But he may give him its own sediment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to the contradiction from step 14, after step 16 rejected the first answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case (different-day sediment versus the wine's own sediment)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on mixing and the permission to give sediment contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban is on sediment from a different batch, and the wine's own sediment may be given.
steps.whatToRemember: Under רב יהודה's reading, the problem is foreign sediment from a different day's wine. The wine's own natural dregs may be passed along.

steps.title: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה supports this reading
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that one pouring wine for another may not mix last night's sediment with today's or the reverse, but may mix same-day with same-day.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this. רבי יהודה says: Someone who pours off wine for his friend may not mix last night's with today's, or today's with last night's. But he may mix last night's with last night's, and today's with today's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב יהודה said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spells out both sides. Mixing across days is forbidden, and mixing within the same day's batch is allowed. This confirms that the משנה's ban is about mixing different batches, as רב יהודה explained.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is also taught this way', bringing a ברייתא in support
One who pours off liquid from the top, leaving the dregs behind

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
One who pours off wine for his friend

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יְעָרֵב שֶׁל אֶמֶשׁ בְּשֶׁל יוֹם,
phrases.english: may not mix that of last night with that of today,
nor that of today with that of last night.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מְעָרֵב שֶׁל אֶמֶשׁ בְּשֶׁל אֶמֶשׁ,
phrases.english: But he may mix that of last night with that of last night,
and that of today with that of today.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's answer from step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's reading that the ban is on mixing sediment from different days
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in the name of רבי יהודה

steps.title: Watered wine, and רבא sends diluted wine back to the store
steps.stepSummary: After quoting the משנה about watered wine, the גמרא tells how רבא diluted store wine, did not like it, and sent it back to the store to be sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If water got mixed into someone's wine, he may not sell it in a store unless he tells the buyer, and so on. They brought רבא wine from a store. He diluted it, tasted it, and it was not good, so he sent it back to the store.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about watered wine and then tells a story about רבא. This story sets up אביי's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's wine was now watered, and he sent it back to a storekeeper, who sells to the public. That looks like selling watered wine to a תגר, which the משנה forbids even when the seller tells him.

phrases.english: One who had water mix into his wine,
may not sell it in the store,
unless he informs him, etc.
They brought Rava wine from a store,
he diluted it, tasted it,
it was not tasty,
he sent it to the store.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה, about watered wine, and gives a story connected to it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Watered wine may be sold in a store only if the buyer is told. רבא returned diluted wine to a store.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה forbids selling to a merchant
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא: the משנה says watered wine may not be given to a תגר even if he is told.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But we learned in the משנה, 'and not to a merchant, even if he told him'!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי questions what רבא did, based on the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A storekeeper is a תגר who resells the wine. The משנה forbids selling him watered wine even with full disclosure, so sending it back to the store seems forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But we learned', which challenges someone from a משנה

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But didn't we learn,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא לַתַּגָּר, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוֹדִיעוֹ!
phrases.english: and not to a merchant, even if he informed him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's action from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא sending diluted wine back to a store
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids giving watered wine to a merchant even with disclosure.

steps.title: רבא: my dilution is obvious
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the way he dilutes wine is clearly noticeable to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My dilution is clearly known.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends what he did by saying no one could be fooled by his watered wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry with a תגר is that he will pass the watered wine on to customers who don't know. רבא's dilution is so plain that any customer would notice, so nobody would be cheated.

keyTerms.meaning: Dilution, a mixing of wine with water

phrases.english: He said to him:
My dilution is clearly known.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any watered wine given to a merchant is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wine so clearly diluted that no one can be fooled is not included in the ban.

steps.title: Worrying about every trick would never end
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the worry that the storekeeper will add wine to hide the water: if we worried about that, there would be no end.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the storekeeper will add more wine, sweeten it, and sell it, then if so, there is no end to the matter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers an objection before anyone raises it: maybe the storekeeper will cover up the dilution and then sell it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could argue that the storekeeper might add wine so the water is no longer noticeable. רבא says that if we worried about that kind of trick, we could never sell anything to any merchant. So we do not worry about it.

keyTerms.meaning: Sweetens it, makes it taste better
There is no end to the matter

phrases.english: And if you say that he adds more
phrases.notes: He means the storekeeper adds more wine so the water is hidden.

phrases.english: and sweetens it and sells it,
if so, there is no end to the matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּטָפֵי וּמְחַיְּילֵיהּ וּמְזַבֵּין לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens רבא's answer in step 21 by setting aside a possible objection.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even obvious dilution might be covered up by the merchant.
steps.terutzMaskana: We do not worry about later tricks, or no sale to a merchant would ever be allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's position: wine that is clearly watered down may go back to a store. We do not worry that the merchant will later disguise it.

steps.title: Where diluting is the custom, and how much water
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows adding water where that is the local custom, and a ברייתא says it may be a half, a third, or a quarter.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: In a place where people usually add water to wine, they may add it, and so on. A ברייתא teaches: a half, a third, or a quarter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's permission to dilute wine where that is the custom, and then adds a ברייתא that gives the amounts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where everyone knows the wine is diluted, adding water is not cheating. The ברייתא explains how much water is meant: a half, a third, or a quarter of the mix, depending on what is done locally.

keyTerms.meaning: A place where it is the custom

phrases.english: In a place where they are accustomed to put water in wine,
they may put it in, etc.
It was taught: for a half, for a third, and for a quarter.
phrases.notes: These are how much of the mixture may be water, depending on the local custom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה, about local custom to dilute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where diluting is the custom, water may be added: a half, a third, or a quarter.

steps.title: רב: this was taught for the winepress stage
steps.stepSummary: רב limits the permission to dilute to the time when the wine is still in the winepresses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: They taught this only about the time the wine is among the winepresses.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a time limit to the permission to add water to wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even where diluting is the custom, the permission applies only while the wine is still fresh in the winepresses. This is very similar to רב נחמן's limit on mixing wines in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They taught', meaning the rule was said about this case

phrases.english: Rav said: And they taught this among the winepresses.
phrases.notes: He means the permission is only while the wine is still fresh in the winepress, like רב נחמן's limit earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the permission given in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Diluting wine by local custom is allowed only during the winepress stage.
steps.whatToRemember: Adding water to wine is allowed only where it is the custom, only in the usual amounts (a half, a third, or a quarter), and, according to רב, only while the wine is in the winepresses.

steps.title: Handing out treats to children
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה forbids a storekeeper to give children toasted grain and nuts, because it draws them to his store. The חכמים permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says a storekeeper may not give out toasted grain and nuts to children, because this gets them used to coming to his store. The חכמים allow it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a disagreement about whether a storekeeper may give free treats to children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה sees the treats as unfair, because they pull customers away from other storekeepers. The חכמים allow it, and the גמרא will explain their reason soon.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. The printed text shortens it to מַתְנִי׳.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
A storekeeper may not hand out
toasted grain and nuts to children,
because he gets them used to coming to him.
And the Rabbis permit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה, moving from watering down wine to fair ways of competing with other sellers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: a storekeeper may not hand out treats to children. חכמים: it is permitted.

steps.title: Lowering the market price
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a seller may not sell below the market price. The חכמים say such a seller should be remembered for good.
steps.simpleTranslation: A seller may not lower the price below the market rate. The חכמים say that if he does, he deserves to be remembered for good.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second disagreement: whether a seller may sell below the going price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view treats lowering prices as unfair to other sellers, just like the treats. The חכמים go further than allowing it. They actually praise him, and the גמרא will ask why.

keyTerms.meaning: Remembered for good, a phrase of praise

phrases.english: And he may not lower the market price,
phrases.notes: This continues רבי יהודה's view from the line before.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: he should be remembered for good.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case in the same משנה about competing with other sellers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First view: a seller may not sell below the market price. חכמים: he is praiseworthy.

steps.title: Sifting ground beans
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול forbids sifting ground beans. The חכמים permit it, but they agree that sifting only the top of the bin is deception.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says one may not sift ground beans to clean out the waste. The חכמים allow it. They agree, though, that one may not sift only the top of the bin, because that just fools the eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to making goods look better, and discusses sifting beans before selling them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול forbids sifting completely. The חכמים allow a real cleaning of the beans. Sifting only the top layer makes the whole bin look clean when it is not, so everyone forbids that.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'stealing the eye': giving a false impression

phrases.english: One may not sift the ground beans,
these are the words of Abba Shaul.
And the Rabbis permit it,
and they agree that he may not sift
only from the opening of the bin,
phrases.notes: He means cleaning just the top layer, so the whole bin looks sifted.

phrases.english: because that is nothing but deceiving the eye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from competing with other sellers to making goods look better.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא שאול forbids sifting. חכמים permit it, except sifting only the top of the bin, which is deception.

steps.title: No dressing up items for sale
steps.stepSummary: One may not dress up a slave, an animal, or vessels to make them look better for sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not make a person, an animal, or vessels look better than they really are in order to sell them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a rule that no one disputes: no dressing up merchandise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows from the same idea as the bin of beans. Making something look better than it really is misleads the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: Dress up or polish to make something look better

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה allows real improvements and fair competition, but it forbids anything that creates a false impression for the buyer.

phrases.english: One may not dress up a person,
phrases.notes: He means a slave being sold.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה, וְלֹא אֶת הַכֵּלִים.
phrases.english: nor an animal, nor vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the ban on deception from beans to any item being sold.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People, animals, and vessels may not be dressed up for sale.

steps.title: Why do the חכמים allow handing out treats?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason of the חכמים, who permit handing out treats to children.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks why the חכמים allow the storekeeper to give treats. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's worry sounds reasonable, since the treats really do pull children to one store. So the גמרא wants to know what the חכמים say to that.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה. The printed text shortens it to גְּמָ׳.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא's first question on the משנה, about its first case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the חכמים are not bothered by the storekeeper drawing children to his store.

steps.title: Everyone can hand out treats
steps.stepSummary: The storekeeper can tell his competitor: I hand out nuts, and you can hand out jujubes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he can say to the other storekeeper: I give out nuts, and you can give out jujubes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this is fair, because every storekeeper can do the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The treats are not unfair because no seller is blocked from using them. Each competitor is free to offer his own treats, so it is open competition.

phrases.english: Because he can say to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the competing storekeeper who complains.

phrases.english: I hand out nuts,
and you hand out jujubes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Every storekeeper can give out treats, so it is fair competition and not stealing customers.

steps.title: Why do the חכמים praise lowering prices?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about lowering prices and asks why the חכמים say such a seller should be remembered for good.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He may not lower the price, and the חכמים say: he should be remembered for good.' What is the reason of the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second case in the משנה and asks for the reason of the חכמים. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the חכמים do more than allow it. They praise him, even though it hurts the other sellers. The question is what good he does that earns this praise.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.: the quote of the משנה continues

phrases.english: "And he may not lower the market price,
and the Rabbis say: he should be remembered for good," etc.
What is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the next line of the משנה and opens a new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the חכמים praise a seller who lowers prices instead of just allowing it.
